title: Preparation of the native input scan
statement: Let $k$ be natural, let $Q,T,S$ be types with decidable equality, let $M$ be a $k$-tape Boolean Turing machine, let $u:T\times\mathrm{Option}(\mathrm{Bool})\to T$, let $N$ be a two-tape Boolean machine with states in $S$, and fix $s_0,s_1\in S$. For a Boolean input word $x$, a four-tape record configuration $d$, a Boolean word $w$, and record data $d_0$, assume that the recorded state is nonempty, the recorded width-one flag is false, $|x|>0$, and $|x|+1<2^{|w|}$. Then there are a Boolean value $b$ and natural numbers $q,t$ such that $b$ records whether the input head of $d$ is at the right boundary $|x|+1$, $q=|x|$ if $b$ and otherwise equals that head position, and $q\le |x|$. The record machine reaches the specified snapshot with its control at the seek stage in state $s_0$, its input head at position zero, and its tape 3 holding the counter word obtained by decrementing the all-true word of length $|w|$ exactly $q+1$ times; the run avoids both verdict states before time $t$, keeps every work-tape head within distance $|w|+1$ of its initial position, and satisfies $t\le 6|w|+5|x|+12$.
hypotheses_covered: fixed start and finish states in $S$
caveat: The formal conclusion refers to private snapshot and record-run constructions; the statement describes their specified control and tape contents.
